Super Mario. Nintendo's flagship platformer franchise debuting in 1985, it follows the adventures of Mario, a plumber who jumps through Mushroom Kingdom levels to rescue Princess Peach from the villainous Bowser. The series revolutionized side-scrolling game design with precise physics, inventive level layouts, and power-ups that remain iconic across gaming. Nintendo created the game in 1985 as an arcade game, then adapted it for the Nintendo Entertainment System in Super Mario Bros., which revitalized the video game industry after the 1983 crash.

The games introduced core mechanics that became industry standards: jumping on enemies, collecting coins, and power-ups like the Super Mushroom, which causes growth, and the Fire Flower, which lets players throw projectiles. Flagpoles mark level completion. Super Mario Bros. 3 in 1988 expanded level design with creative themes, suits like the Raccoon, Frog, and Tanuki forms, and a world-spanning structure.

Super Mario 64 in 1996 pioneered three-dimensional platforming on the Nintendo 64. It featured analog stick control and dynamic camera, influencing a generation of three-dimensional games. Super Mario Galaxy released on the Wii as two games from 2007 to 2010, bringing gravity-shifting mechanics and spherical level design. More recent entries like Super Mario Odyssey in 2017 introduce possession mechanics via the hat companion Cappy. Super Mario Bros. Wonder in 2023 returns to two-dimensional gameplay with dreamlike visual themes.

The franchise spans multiple genres: racing through Mario Kart, sports games, RPGs, and party games. Mario is Nintendo's de facto mascot. Luigi is Mario's brother and frequent co-star in multi-player adventures. Princess Peach, though initially the kidnapped objective across most games, has become a playable character herself. Bowser stands as the Koopa King, Mario's arch-rival and Princess Peach's abductor. Nintendo, the publisher and creator, has made Mario define their brand identity and revolutionized platformer physics and level design.
